transcript: The other night, AJ and I saw an absolutely amazing production of Jelly's Last Jam at New York City Center. Now, I wasn't born yet to see the original 1992 production, and I didn't know much about this going in, but it's somewhat of a bio jukebox musical about the jazz pianist and composer Jelly Roll Morton. At the beginning of the musical, Jelly is introduced after having just died and we see a retelling of his life through his lens and the lens of a mysterious narrator-like figure, here played by Billy Porter. This production was outstanding — the direction is gorgeous, the tap dancing is amazing, as are the performances by an all around stacked cast. This is definitely one of the best Encores productions that I've seen. Especially Act 1, which is packed with what feels like showstopper after showstopper. The music and the live orchestra is thrilling even from the fifth row of the balcony. I was also so so impressed by Nicholas Christopher who plays Jelly. I previously had the pleasure of seeing him play Sweeney Todd just last month but this production really cements him as a triple threat. Jelly's Last Jam as a musical, like many of the musicals produced for the Encores series, is not perfect, but this production and these performances are probably as close as you can get. It’s running only through this Sunday so do not wait if you're trying to catch it before it closes. Side note though, I would love to see this transfer to Broadway and I'm still also hoping for a transfer of last summer's Piazza — but I digress. With that, another program for my collection.
